claims.value: Bodart: side A 14,000 at the end and 41 heavy guns under Mortier; side B 6,000 and 230 guns under Loucadou, later Gneisenau, with Nettelbeck’s citizens.
claims.rationale: Read on the registered page image. His general rule is forces disposable for the engagement, rounded upward (shared research-conventions index); a stated siege endpoint or engaged subset takes precedence over treating it as an opening count. Population/timing alternatives are not reconciled. English rendering (ours): "The Prussian garrison, 6,000 men with 230 guns, initially under Colonel von Loucadou and since May under Major von Gneisenau, strongly supported by the citizens led by mayor J. Nettelbeck, holds out successfully against Mortier’s French besieging army. At the end this numbered 14,000 with 41 heavy guns, half consisting of Italian, Dutch and Rhine troops."

claims.value: Napoleon’s 20 April letter anticipates more than 8,000 before Kolberg by the recipient’s reading, distinct from Bodart’s 14,000 endpoint.
claims.rationale: Superior’s forecast of assembled strength, not confirmed present or engaged count. English rendering (ours): "On the other hand I have reinforced the siege of Kolberg so that, when you read this letter, I shall have more than 8,000 men there."

citations.quote: D’un autre côté, j’ai renforcé le siège de Colberg, de sorte que, lorsque vous lirez cette lettre, j’y aurai plus de 8,000 hommes.

claims.value: Napoleon identifies Loison at the siege and orders allied reinforcements; Mortier’s corps-level label differs from local siege direction.
claims.rationale: Letter continuation, exact dateline not assigned from a neighbouring heading. Reinforcement intentions do not prove arrival. English rendering (ours): "Loison is an active man. He still has two Italian regiments; I am sending him two Württemberg regiments, a Polish regiment and the Saxons of Weimar"

claims.value: Höpfner says the king made Gneisenau successor to Loucadou; the king’s 25 April instruction put Schill’s remaining troops entirely under the commandant.
claims.rationale: The full p 577 paragraph explicitly calls Gneisenau successor. The 25 April royal order printed in p 578’s note precedes Bodart’s “since May” summary; exact arrival/assumption requires a dated record. Nettelbeck’s civic role is not army command. English rendering (ours): "Colonel Lucadou, in Major Gneisenau" English rendering (ours): "The remaining troops of the said corps now remain entirely subject to the commandant’s orders" English rendering (ours): "to give Colonel Lucadou a successor as commandant in Major Gneisenau, in whose ability special confidence was placed"
